message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1978 | **Halloween** (John Carpenter) | The original slasher that set the genre’s tone. |
| 1980 | **The Shining** (Stanley Kubrick) | A psychological masterpiece based on Stephen King’s novel. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** (Wes Craven) | Introduces Freddy Krueger and the terror of dreams. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** (Jonathan Demme) | A chilling crime‑thriller with an iconic villain. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** (Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez) | Pioneered found‑footage horror. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (Danny Boyle) | Revitalized the zombie genre with fast‑moving infected. |
| 2004 | **Saw** (James Wan & Leigh Whannell) | Dark, twisted puzzles that sparked a franchise. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** (Oren Peli) | Low‑budget found footage that made a huge splash. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (James Wan) | A modern supernatural thriller grounded in real events. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (Dennis Dugan & Joss Whedon) | A meta‑take on horror tropes. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** (David Robert Mitchell) | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” concept. |
| 2015 | **Get Out** (Jordan Peele) | A socially conscious horror that won an Oscar. |
| 2017 | **Hereditary** (Ari Aster) | A slow‑burning dread that culminates in a shocking finale. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (John Krasinski) | Silent tension and inventive sound design. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** (Ari Aster) | Daylight horror that subverts expectations. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** (Leigh Whannell) | A modern retelling with strong feminist themes. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** (Nia DaCosta) | A contemporary reimagining of a classic legend. |
| 2022 | **Nope** (Jordan Peele) | A blend of sci‑fi and horror with a satirical edge. |
| 2023 | **Evil Dead Rise** (Lee Cronin) | A fresh entry in the long‑running franchise. |

Feel free to let me know if you’d like recommendations tailored to a particular era, sub‑genre, or director!
